Microfluidic devices handle fluids in channels tens to hundreds of micrometres wide, where flows are laminar and surface-to-volume ratios are high. Segmented gas-liquid flow in such channels creates well-defined interfaces whose evolution can be imaged directly, which makes microfluidics a fast, low-volume way to measure gas solubility, mass transfer and reaction in liquids.

## Gas plug shrinkage as a CO2 solvent screen (2015)

Hallenbeck and coworkers formed pure CO2 plugs at a Y-junction of a glass serpentine microreactor and tracked a single plug with a 500 Hz camera, converting its volume loss into absorbed CO2 via the ideal gas law ([Hallenbeck et al. 2015](/papers/hallenbeck2015/)). The method ranked MEA and four potassium amino acid salts by loading and initial flux using less than a millilitre of solution, and the capacity ranking of lysinate versus MEA matched stirred-reactor breakthrough tests. Measured fluxes (about 0.25 to 0.52 mol m<sup>-2</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>) far exceed wetted-wall values and the capacities were lower than equilibrium values, so absolute numbers are setup specific and the method is best used for relative ranking. Summary: [hallenbeck2015](/papers/hallenbeck2015/).
